about: Error signatures for `rn-buddy why`. Each entry: id, area (one of areas), patterns (regex strings, matched with `flags`, default "i"),
title (what happened, in plain English), causes, fixes, and optional then, learn (a `rn-buddy learn` topic), clean (a `rn-buddy clean --<level>`),
docs (a URL), probe (a project check in src/lib/errors.js), defaults (values for placeholders a pattern may not capture),
kind ("wrapper": a generic 'the build failed' line, "warning": not fatal) and expo (causes/fixes/then to use in Expo projects instead).
List the most specific pattern first: the first pattern that matches fills the placeholders.
Named groups like (?<module>...) fill {module} in the text. Always available: {install} {reinstall} {start} {resetCache} {runAndroid} {runIos} {podExec} {podInstall} {appId}.
Put commands in `backticks` so they stand out.

patterns: Unable to resolve module [`'"]?(?<module>[^\s`'"]+)[`'"]?(?: from [`'"]?(?<from>(?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^:`'"\n]+))?
errors.title: Metro can't find {module}.
causes: The package isn't installed, or was installed while Metro was running
The import path has a typo, or the wrong upper/lower case (macOS forgives that, Android builds and CI don't)
Metro's cache is out of date
fixes: If it's a package: `{install} {module}`
If it's one of your files: check the path and its spelling
errors.then: Restart Metro with a clean cache: `{resetCache}`

patterns: No bundle URL present
errors.title: The iOS app couldn't get its JavaScript from Metro.
causes: Metro isn't running
The app was built while Metro was on another port, or Metro crashed
On a real iPhone: the phone and your computer aren't on the same Wi-Fi, or Local Network access is off for the app
fixes: Start Metro in the project folder and keep it open: `{start}`
Then build and run the app again: `{runIos}`
On a real iPhone: same Wi-Fi, and Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network → allow the app

patterns: Unable to load script\.? Make sure you(?:'|’)re either running Metro
Could not connect to development server
errors.title: The app couldn't reach Metro to load your JavaScript.
causes: Metro isn't running
Android: the device can't reach port 8081 on your computer (the port isn't forwarded)
A real phone is on another Wi-Fi network than your computer
fixes: Start Metro in the project folder: `{start}`
Android: forward the port to the device: `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081`
Then reload: press r in the Metro terminal

patterns: EADDRINUSE:? address already in use \S*?:(?<port>\d+)
Port (?<port>\d+) is (?:already in use|being used by another process)
errors.title: Port {port} is already taken, so Metro can't start.
causes: Another Metro is still running, in an old terminal or for another project
Another program uses port {port}
fixes: See what uses it: `lsof -i :{port}` (Windows: `netstat -ano | findstr :{port}`)
Close that terminal, or stop the process: `kill <PID>`
Or run Metro on another port: `npx react-native start --port 8082`, and the app with `--port 8082` too

patterns: "(?<app>[^"]+)" has not been registered
Application (?<app>\S+) has not been registered
errors.title: The native app asked for a component named "{app}", but your JavaScript didn't register it.
causes: Metro is running from another project folder
The name in index.js (AppRegistry.registerComponent) differs from the one the native app asks for (getMainComponentName in MainActivity, withModuleName in AppDelegate)
An error earlier stopped index.js before it registered the app: look for the first red error above this one
fixes: Stop every Metro, then start it in this project: `{resetCache}`
Use the same name everywhere: index.js registers the name from app.json

causes: An error while loading your app stopped it before it registered: look for the first red error above this one
"main" in package.json points to the wrong file (Expo Router projects use "expo-router/entry")
Metro is running from another project folder
fixes: Fix the first error in the log
Check "main" in package.json
Restart with a clean cache: `npx expo start --clear`

patterns: Recrawled this watch \d+ times?
errors.title: Watchman lost track of your files and had to rescan the project.
causes: Many files changed at once (a git checkout, npm install)
Watchman's saved state is out of date
fixes: Reset Watchman: `watchman watch-del-all`, then `watchman shutdown-server`

patterns: EMFILE: too many open files
ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached
errors.title: Metro ran out of file watchers.
causes: Watchman isn't installed, so Node watches every file itself
Linux: the system limit for watched files (inotify) is too low
fixes: macOS: install Watchman: `brew install watchman`
Linux: raise the limit: `echo fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf && sudo sysctl -p`

patterns: TypeError: Network request failed
errors.title: A fetch() call couldn't reach the server.
causes: The URL uses localhost: on an Android emulator that's the emulator itself, on a phone it's the phone
The URL is http:// and the platform blocks plain HTTP (Android release builds, iOS unless allowed in Info.plist)
The server isn't running, or the device is offline
fixes: Android emulator: use http://10.0.2.2:<port> instead of localhost, or forward the port: `adb reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>`
Real phone: use your computer's IP address on the same Wi-Fi, or an https:// URL
Use https:// for real servers

patterns: ReferenceError: Property '(?<name>[^']+)' doesn't exist
errors.title: Your code uses {name}, but nothing named {name} exists where it runs.
causes: A typo, or a missing import of {name}
{name} is a browser or Node.js global that React Native doesn't have (like localStorage, document or Buffer)
fixes: Find {name} in your code (the stack trace under the error shows the file) and import or declare it
For browser/Node globals, use a React Native package instead (e.g. @react-native-async-storage/async-storage for localStorage)

patterns: TurboModuleRegistry\.getEnforcing\(\.\.\.\): '(?<module>[^']+)' could not be found
errors.title: The native module {module} isn't in the app you're running.
causes: A package with native code was installed, but the app wasn't rebuilt (reloading only updates JavaScript)
iOS: pod install wasn't run after installing it
In Expo Go: the package needs native code that Expo Go doesn't have
fixes: iOS: `{podInstall}`
Rebuild the app: `{runAndroid}` or `{runIos}`

patterns: requireNativeComponent: "(?<module>[^"]+)" was not found in the UIManager
Unimplemented component: <(?<module>[^>]+)>
errors.title: The native view {module} isn't in the app you're running.
causes: A package with native code was installed, but the app wasn't rebuilt (reloading only updates JavaScript)
iOS: pod install wasn't run after installing it
The package doesn't support the New Architecture ("Unimplemented component")
fixes: iOS: `{podInstall}`
Rebuild the app: `{runAndroid}` or `{runIos}`

patterns: null is not an object \(evaluating '[\w$.]*?NativeModules\.(?<module>\w+)
The package '(?<module>[^']+)' doesn't seem to be linked
NativeModule: (?<module>\w+) is null
Native module cannot be null
errors.title: The native code for {module} isn't in the app you're running.
causes: A package with native code was installed, but the app wasn't rebuilt (reloading only updates JavaScript)
iOS: pod install wasn't run after installing it
In Expo Go: the package needs native code that Expo Go doesn't have
fixes: iOS: `{podInstall}`
Rebuild the app: `{runAndroid}` or `{runIos}`

patterns: Cannot find native module '(?<module>[^']+)'
tried to access a native module that doesn't exist
not (?:available|supported) in Expo Go
removed from Expo Go
errors.title: The native code for {module} isn't in the app you're running (Expo Go, or an old development build).
causes: Expo Go only has the native code of the Expo SDK. Packages with other native code need a development build
You added a package with native code after making your development build
fixes: Make a development build: `npx expo install expo-dev-client`, then `npx expo run:android` or `npx expo run:ios` (or in the cloud: `eas build --profile development`)
Then open the project in it, not in Expo Go: `npx expo start` (press s to switch)

patterns: Project is incompatible with this version of Expo Go
requires a newer version of Expo Go
errors.title: The Expo Go app and this project use different Expo SDK versions.
causes: Expo Go from the app stores only runs the latest SDK
This project uses an older (or newer) SDK
fixes: Upgrade the project to the latest SDK: `npx expo install expo@latest --fix`
Or use a development build, which works with any SDK: `npx expo run:android` or `npx expo run:ios`
On an emulator or simulator, `npx expo start` can install the matching Expo Go for you (press a or i)

patterns: The following packages should be updated for best compatibility with the installed expo version
Some dependencies are incompatible with the installed expo version
errors.title: Some packages don't match the versions your Expo SDK expects.
causes: Packages were installed with npm install, which takes the latest version, instead of npx expo install, which picks the one for your SDK
Expo was upgraded, but the other packages weren't
fixes: See which ones: `npx expo install --check`
Fix them: `npx expo install --fix`
errors.then: Restart with a clean cache: `npx expo start --clear`

patterns: No development build \((?<appId>[^)]+)\) for this project is installed
errors.title: There's no development build of this app ({appId}) on the device.
causes: The project has expo-dev-client, so `npx expo start` opens a development build, and none is installed yet
It was uninstalled, or you're using another emulator or simulator
fixes: Build and install it: `npx expo run:android` or `npx expo run:ios` (or `eas build --profile development`)
Or open the project in Expo Go instead: `npx expo start`, then press s

patterns: SDK location not found
errors.title: Gradle can't find the Android SDK.
causes: ANDROID_HOME isn't set where the build runs
android/local.properties doesn't exist or has no sdk.dir line
fixes: Set ANDROID_HOME in your shell profile (~/.zshrc): `export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk` (Linux: $HOME/Android/Sdk), then open a new terminal
Or create android/local.properties with the line `sdk.dir=/Users/<you>/Library/Android/sdk`

patterns: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory
JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found
errors.title: Gradle can't find Java: JAVA_HOME is wrong or not set.
causes: JAVA_HOME points to a folder that doesn't exist (a JDK that was removed or updated)
No JDK is installed
fixes: Install JDK 17, the version React Native recommends: `brew install --cask zulu@17`
Point JAVA_HOME at it in ~/.zshrc: `export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-17.jdk/Contents/Home`, then open a new terminal

patterns: Unsupported class file major version (?<major>\d+)
errors.title: Gradle ran with a JDK that's too new for it (class file major version {major}).
causes: Gradle uses JAVA_HOME (or java on your PATH), and that JDK is newer than this Gradle version supports
React Native's Android build expects JDK 17
fixes: Install JDK 17 and point JAVA_HOME at it: `export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-17.jdk/Contents/Home`
Stop Gradle daemons that still use the old JDK: `cd android && ./gradlew --stop`

patterns: Android Gradle plugin requires Java (?<wanted>\d+) to run\. You are currently using Java (?<current>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)
Gradle requires JVM (?<wanted>\d+) or later to run\. Your build is currently configured to use JVM (?<current>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)
Your build is currently configured to use incompatible Java (?<current>\d+(?:\.\d+)*) and Gradle
errors.title: The Android build needs Java {wanted}, but it runs with Java {current}.
causes: JAVA_HOME (or java on your PATH) points to another JDK
Android Studio uses its own Gradle JDK setting
fixes: Install JDK 17 and point JAVA_HOME at it: `export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-17.jdk/Contents/Home`
Android Studio: Settings → Build, Execution, Deployment → Build Tools → Gradle → Gradle JDK
Stop old Gradle daemons: `cd android && ./gradlew --stop`

patterns: INSTALL_FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE
errors.title: The device or emulator is out of storage, so the app can't be installed.
causes: Emulators start with little internal storage, and every build adds up
fixes: Emulator: Android Studio → Device Manager → ⋮ → Wipe Data, or edit the device and give it more internal storage
Phone: free up space, or remove the old build: `adb uninstall {appId}`

patterns: INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE(?:: Existing package (?<appId>[\w.]+) signatures do not match)?
errors.title: An app with the same ID ({appId}) but signed with another key is already installed.
causes: A release build, or a build from another computer, is installed, and debug builds are signed with a different key
fixes: Uninstall the old app (this deletes its data): `adb uninstall {appId}`

patterns: Duplicate class (?<class>\S+) found in modules?
errors.title: Two libraries both contain the class {class}.
causes: Two packages bring different versions of the same Android library
An old package still uses the Android Support Library while the app uses AndroidX
Kotlin standard library versions clash (kotlin-stdlib and kotlin-stdlib-jdk8)
fixes: See which packages bring it: `cd android && ./gradlew app:dependencies --configuration debugRuntimeClasspath`
Update the package that brings the old version (`npm outdated`), or replace it if it's unmaintained
Then clean: `cd android && ./gradlew clean`

patterns: \d+ files found with path 'lib/[^/']+/(?<lib>[^']+)'
Execution failed for task ':app:merge\w*NativeLibs'
errors.title: Two packages contain the same native file ({lib}), and Gradle doesn't know which one to keep.
causes: Two packages ship their own copy of the same .so file (often libc++_shared.so or libfbjni.so)
An old package ships native files of an older React Native
fixes: Update the packages named in the lines after this error
If they are up to date, keep one copy: in android/app/build.gradle, inside android { }, add `packaging { jniLibs { pickFirsts += ['**/{lib}'] } }`
Then clean: `cd android && ./gradlew clean`

patterns: \[CXX1101\] NDK at \S*?(?<ndk>\d+(?:\.\d+)*) did not have a source\.properties file
No version of NDK matched the requested version (?<ndk>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)
NDK is not installed
NDK not configured
errors.title: The Android NDK this project needs ({ndk}) isn't installed, or its download is broken.
causes: React Native compiles C++ code with the NDK version set as ndkVersion in android/build.gradle
An NDK download was interrupted, leaving a folder without source.properties
fixes: Android Studio → Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Android SDK → SDK Tools → tick Show Package Details → NDK (Side by side) → {ndk}
Or in a terminal: `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager "ndk;{ndk}"`
A broken download: delete $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/{ndk} and install it again

patterns: No connected devices
Make sure you have an Android emulator running or a device connected
no devices/emulators found
errors.title: No Android emulator is running and no phone is connected.
causes: The emulator isn't started
The phone isn't plugged in with USB debugging on, or you didn't accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt
fixes: See what adb sees: `adb devices`
Start an emulator: `rn-buddy device start`, or Android Studio → Device Manager → ▶
Phone: Settings → Developer options → USB debugging on, plug it in and accept the prompt

patterns: device unauthorized
errors.title: Your phone is connected, but it hasn't allowed USB debugging from this computer yet.
causes: The "Allow USB debugging?" prompt on the phone wasn't accepted
fixes: Unlock the phone and accept the prompt (tick Always allow)
No prompt? Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations, then unplug and plug in again
Check: `adb devices` should say device, not unauthorized

patterns: command not found: (?<tool>adb|emulator)\b
(?:^|\s)(?<tool>adb|emulator): command not found
'(?<tool>adb|emulator)' is not recognized as an internal or external command
spawn (?<tool>adb|emulator) ENOENT
errors.title: Your terminal can't find the Android tool {tool}.
causes: The Android SDK's platform-tools and emulator folders aren't on your PATH
ANDROID_HOME isn't set
fixes: Add to ~/.zshrc: `export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk` and `export PATH=$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/emulator:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools`
Then open a new terminal and check: `adb --version`

patterns: some licen[cs]es have not been accepted
You have not accepted the license agreements of the following SDK components
errors.title: The Android SDK licenses aren't accepted, so Gradle can't download what the build needs.
causes: A new SDK component is needed, and its license was never accepted on this computer
fixes: Accept them: `yes | $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager --licenses`
No cmdline-tools folder? Android Studio → SDK Manager → SDK Tools → Android SDK Command-line Tools

patterns: OutOfMemoryError: (?:Java heap space|Metaspace)
Expiring Daemon because JVM heap space is exhausted
Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly
errors.title: Gradle ran out of memory.
causes: The Gradle daemon has less memory than the build needs
Android Studio, an emulator and Gradle together use a lot of RAM
fixes: In android/gradle.properties, set `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4096m -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1024m`
Stop old daemons: `cd android && ./gradlew --stop`
Close apps you don't need while building

patterns: Module was compiled with an incompatible version of Kotlin\. The binary version of its metadata is (?<found>\d+(?:\.\d+)*), expected version is (?<expected>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)
errors.title: A library was built with Kotlin {found}, but your build uses Kotlin {expected}.
causes: The library version is newer than your React Native version supports
fixes: Install a version of the library that matches your React Native version (see its README or changelog)
Or upgrade React Native, which brings a newer Kotlin: `rn-buddy upgrade`
Then clean: `cd android && ./gradlew clean`

patterns: uses-sdk:minSdkVersion (?<current>\d+) cannot be smaller than version (?<wanted>\d+) declared in library (?<lib>\S+)
errors.title: A library needs minSdkVersion {wanted}, but your app is set to {current}.
causes: The library dropped support for older Android versions
fixes: Raise minSdkVersion to {wanted} in android/build.gradle (buildscript → ext)
Or use an older version of the library that still supports {current}
Raise it with expo-build-properties: `npx expo install expo-build-properties`, then in app.json plugins: `["expo-build-properties", { "android": { "minSdkVersion": {wanted} } }]`
Or use an older version of the library that still supports {current}
expo.then: Make a new build: `npx expo prebuild --clean`, then `npx expo run:android`

patterns: to compile against version (?<wanted>\d+) or later of the\s+Android APIs
errors.title: A library needs compileSdkVersion {wanted} or newer.
causes: The library was made for a newer React Native, which compiles against a newer Android SDK
fixes: Raise compileSdkVersion to {wanted} in android/build.gradle (buildscript → ext) and install Android SDK Platform {wanted} in Android Studio → SDK Manager
Or use an older version of the library, or upgrade React Native: `rn-buddy upgrade`
Raise it with expo-build-properties: `npx expo install expo-build-properties`, then in app.json plugins: `["expo-build-properties", { "android": { "compileSdkVersion": {wanted} } }]`
Or use the library version that `npx expo install` picks for your SDK
expo.then: Make a new build: `npx expo prebuild --clean`, then `npx expo run:android`

patterns: Could not resolve all (?:files|dependencies|artifacts) for configuration
errors.title: Gradle couldn't download {dep}.
causes: No internet, a proxy or VPN in the way, or the Maven repository was down
An old package asks for a version that doesn't exist anymore (jcenter() shut down)
Gradle is in offline mode
fixes: Check your connection, then retry with fresh downloads: `cd android && ./gradlew app:assembleDebug --refresh-dependencies`
If an old package asks for it, update that package

patterns: Execution failed for task '(?<task>[^']+)'
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception
BUILD FAILED in
Failed to install the app\. Command failed with exit code \d+: \S*gradlew
errors.title: The Android build failed. This line only says that it failed: the cause is printed above it.
causes: The real error is in the "What went wrong:" block, or in the first lines that start with "e:" or "error:"
fixes: Build again with details: `cd android && ./gradlew app:assembleDebug --stacktrace`
Pipe the whole log into rn-buddy: `{runAndroid} 2>&1 | rn-buddy why`

patterns: CocoaPods could not find compatible versions for pod "(?<pod>[^"]+)"
errors.title: CocoaPods can't find a version of {pod} that fits every requirement.
causes: ios/Podfile.lock pins an older {pod}, and a package you updated needs a newer one
The list of pods on your computer (the spec repo) is out of date
A pod needs a newer iOS version than the platform :ios line in the Podfile
fixes: Update the list of pods: `(cd ios && {podExec} install --repo-update)`
Or let CocoaPods update only that pod: `(cd ios && {podExec} update {pod})`

patterns: required a higher minimum deployment target
errors.title: A pod needs a newer iOS version than this app's minimum.
causes: The package (or its version) needs a newer iOS than the platform :ios line in ios/Podfile
fixes: Use a version of the package that matches your React Native version
Or raise the minimum in ios/Podfile, e.g. `platform :ios, '16.0'` instead of `platform :ios, min_ios_version_supported`, only if the package's docs ask for it
Raise it with expo-build-properties: `npx expo install expo-build-properties`, then in app.json plugins: `["expo-build-properties", { "ios": { "deploymentTarget": "16.0" } }]`
Or use the version that `npx expo install` picks for your SDK
expo.then: Make a new build: `npx expo prebuild --clean`, then `npx expo run:ios`

patterns: The sandbox is not in sync with the Podfile\.lock
errors.title: The installed pods (ios/Pods) don't match ios/Podfile.lock.
causes: You pulled changes or installed packages but didn't run pod install
fixes: `{podInstall}`
Then build again, from ios/<App>.xcworkspace (not .xcodeproj)

patterns: Could not find 'bundler' \((?<version>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\) required by
errors.title: The Bundler version that Gemfile.lock asks for ({version}) isn't installed.
causes: Gemfile.lock was made with another Bundler version than the one on this computer
fixes: Install it: `gem install bundler:{version}`
Then install the gems: `bundle install`

patterns: Could not find gem '(?<gem>[^']+)' in locally installed gems
Could not find (?<gem>[\w-]+-\d[\w.]*) in locally installed gems
bundler: command not found: pod
errors.title: The Ruby gems this project needs ({gem}) aren't installed.
causes: `bundle install` wasn't run after cloning the project, or after the Gemfile changed
fixes: In the project folder: `bundle install`

patterns: Sandbox: rsync(?:\.samba)?\(\d+\) deny\(1\) file-
errors.title: Xcode's script sandbox stopped a build script from copying files.
causes: Xcode turns on User Script Sandboxing (ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING), and a build phase script copies files
fixes: In Xcode: select the app target → Build Settings → search "User Script Sandboxing" → set it to No
Then Product → Clean Build Folder (⇧⌘K) and build again

patterns: Can't find the '[^']*' binary to build the React Native bundle
line \d+: node: command not found
env: node: No such file or directory
errors.title: Xcode can't find Node, so it can't bundle your JavaScript.
causes: Xcode doesn't load your shell profile, so a Node installed with nvm, fnm, asdf or volta isn't on its PATH
fixes: Tell Xcode where Node is: `echo export NODE_BINARY=$(command -v node) > ios/.xcode.env.local`

patterns: Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code
\*\* BUILD FAILED \*\*
"xcodebuild" exited with error code
Failed to build ios project
The following build commands failed:
errors.title: The iOS build failed. This line only says that it failed: the cause is printed above it.
causes: A build step failed: often "Bundle React Native code and images" (a JavaScript error, or Xcode can't find Node) or a "[CP]" step (pods out of date)
fixes: Look above for the first line with "error:"
Or build in Xcode to see the failing step: `xed ios`, ⌘B, then the Report navigator (⌘9)
Pipe the whole log into rn-buddy: `{runIos} 2>&1 | rn-buddy why`

patterns: Multiple commands produce '(?<file>[^']+)'
errors.title: Two build steps write the same file: {file}.
causes: A font or resource is in Copy Bundle Resources and is also copied by a pod (react-native-vector-icons fonts are the classic case)
A file was added to the target twice
fixes: In Xcode: app target → Build Phases → Copy Bundle Resources: remove the duplicate
Then Product → Clean Build Folder (⇧⌘K)

patterns: No such module '(?<module>[^']+)'
errors.title: Xcode can't find the module {module}.
causes: The .xcodeproj was opened instead of the .xcworkspace, so Xcode doesn't see the pods
pod install wasn't run after installing a package
Old build data
fixes: `{podInstall}`
Open the workspace, not the project: `xed ios`
Product → Clean Build Folder (⇧⌘K)

patterns: Undefined symbols? for architecture (?<arch>\w+)
linker command failed with exit code 1
errors.title: The linker couldn't find code the app uses.
causes: Pods are missing or out of date
The .xcodeproj was built instead of the .xcworkspace
A package doesn't support your React Native version or the New Architecture
fixes: `{podInstall}`
Build the workspace: `xed ios`
Product → Clean Build Folder (⇧⌘K)

patterns: accessing build database .*database is locked
errors.title: Another Xcode build of this app is still running.
causes: Xcode and a terminal (or two terminals) are building at the same time
fixes: Wait for the other build or stop it (■ in Xcode, Ctrl+C in the terminal)
Still locked? Quit Xcode and build again

patterns: Unable to boot (?:the )?Simulator
Unable to lookup in current state: Shutdown
errors.title: The iOS Simulator couldn't start.
causes: The simulator is stuck from an earlier run
The iOS runtime for that simulator isn't installed
The disk is almost full
fixes: Shut down all simulators and try again: `xcrun simctl shutdown all`
Install the runtime: Xcode → Settings → Components
Still stuck? Erase it, which deletes its apps and data: `xcrun simctl erase <device id>`

patterns: Could not find "(?<name>[^"]+)" simulator
No simulator available with name "(?<name>[^"]+)"
errors.title: There's no simulator named "{name}".
causes: That device isn't installed in this Xcode version
fixes: List your simulators: `xcrun simctl list devices available`
Run on one of them: `npx react-native run-ios --simulator "iPhone 16"`
Or add one in Xcode → Window → Devices and Simulators
List your simulators: `xcrun simctl list devices available`
Pick one when building: `npx expo run:ios --device`

patterns: Signing for "(?<target>[^"]+)" requires a development team
errors.title: Xcode needs a signing team to build {target} for a real iPhone.
causes: No Team is chosen for the target. A free Personal Team (your Apple ID) is enough for your own phone
fixes: `xed ios` → select the {target} target → Signing & Capabilities → Team → pick your Apple ID (Add an Account... if it isn't there)
Only testing? The Simulator needs no signing: `{runIos}`

patterns: No profiles for '(?<bundleId>[^']+)' were found
errors.title: Xcode has no provisioning profile for the bundle ID {bundleId}.
causes: Automatic signing is off, or no Team is chosen
With a free Personal Team the bundle ID must be unique, and someone else already uses it
fixes: Signing & Capabilities → tick Automatically manage signing and choose your Team
Change the bundle ID to one only you use, e.g. com.yourname.myapp: `rn-buddy app id com.yourname.myapp`

patterns: requires Xcode, but active developer directory '[^']+' is a command line tools instance
SDK "iphoneos" cannot be located
unable to find utility "(?:simctl|xcodebuild)", not a developer tool or in PATH
errors.title: Your terminal uses the Command Line Tools instead of the full Xcode.
causes: xcode-select points to /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools, which can't build iOS apps
fixes: Point it to Xcode: `sudo xcode-select --switch /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`
Accept the license and finish the setup: `sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`

patterns: (?<platform>iOS \d+(?:\.\d+)*) is not installed\. To use with Xcode, first download and install the platform
iOS [\d.]+ Platform Not Installed
errors.title: The {platform} platform isn't installed in Xcode.
causes: Xcode downloads iOS platforms separately, and this one isn't there yet
fixes: Xcode → Settings → Components → install the iOS platform
Or in a terminal: `xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS`

patterns: Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component
errors.title: Some text is placed directly inside a <View> (or another component that isn't <Text>).
causes: A string or number in JSX outside <Text>
`count && <Item />` where count is 0 or "": React renders the 0 or "" as text
A stray character in JSX, like a ; or a space after a closing tag
fixes: Wrap the text: `<Text>Hello</Text>`
Use a real true/false in conditions: `count > 0 && <Item />`, or `name ? <Item /> : null`

patterns: VirtualizedLists should never be nested inside plain ScrollViews with the same orientation
errors.title: A FlatList (or SectionList) is inside a ScrollView that scrolls the same way.
causes: The outer ScrollView makes the list render every item at once, so it loses its speed
fixes: Remove the ScrollView and move the other content into the list's ListHeaderComponent and ListFooterComponent
For a short list, render the items with .map() instead of a FlatList

patterns: Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop
errors.title: Items rendered from an array need a unique key.
causes: An element returned from .map() has no key, or two items have the same key
fixes: Add a key to the outer element in .map(): `items.map((item) => <Row key={item.id} title={item.title} />)`
FlatList: `keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}`
Use a stable id, not the array index, when items can move

patterns: Rendered (?:more|fewer) hooks than (?:during the previous render|expected)
errors.title: A component called a different number of hooks than in its last render.
causes: A hook is inside an if, a loop, or after an early return
A hook is called inside a callback
fixes: Move every hook (useState, useEffect, your useSomething) to the top of the component, before any return
Put the condition inside the hook instead: `useEffect(() => { if (ready) load(); }, [ready])`

patterns: Invalid hook call\. Hooks can only be called inside (?:of )?the body of a function component
errors.title: A hook was called somewhere React doesn't allow it.
causes: The hook is called in a regular function, a class component or an event handler
Two copies of React are installed
react doesn't match the version react-native needs
fixes: Call hooks only at the top of function components and of custom hooks named useSomething
Check for duplicate React: `npm ls react`

patterns: Too many re-renders\. React limits the number of renders to prevent an infinite loop
errors.title: A component sets state while it renders, which renders it again, forever.
causes: `onPress={setOpen(true)}` calls the function while rendering instead of passing it
setState is called directly in the component body
fixes: Pass a function: `onPress={() => setOpen(true)}`
Move state updates into an event handler or a useEffect

patterns: Maximum update depth exceeded
errors.title: State updates keep triggering each other in a loop.
causes: A useEffect sets state that's in its own dependency list
An object, array or function made during render is used as a useEffect dependency, so it's new every time
fixes: Check each useEffect that calls a setter: does it change one of its own dependencies?
Wrap objects and functions used as dependencies in useMemo or useCallback, or only set state when the value changed

patterns: Cannot update a component \(`(?<other>[^`]+)`\) while rendering a different component \(`(?<current>[^`]+)`\)
errors.title: {current} changes the state of {other} while it renders.
causes: A setter from a parent (or a store update) is called in {current}'s body instead of in an effect or event
fixes: Move the update into a useEffect, or into the event handler that causes it

patterns: Element type is invalid: expected a string \(for built-in components\) or a class/function \(for composite components\) but got: (?<got>\w+)
errors.title: You're rendering a component that is {got}, usually because of a wrong import.
causes: Default and named imports are mixed up: `import Button from './Button'` vs `import { Button } from './Button'`
The component isn't exported from its file
A typo in the imported name
fixes: The error says "Check the render method of X": look at the imports in X
Match the import to the export: `export default Button` ↔ `import Button`, `export function Button` ↔ `import { Button }`

patterns: Objects are not valid as a React child
errors.title: You're rendering an object (or a Promise) directly in JSX.
causes: A whole object is put in JSX instead of one of its fields
An async function's result (a Promise) is rendered
fixes: Render one field: `<Text>{user.name}</Text>`, not the whole user object
To look at it: `<Text>{JSON.stringify(value)}</Text>`
Load async data in a useEffect and keep the result in state

patterns: The action '(?<action>\w+)' with payload .*? was not handled by any navigator
errors.title: React Navigation couldn't {action}: no navigator around this screen has that screen name.
causes: The screen name is misspelled, or not registered with <Stack.Screen name="...">
The screen is in a nested navigator: navigate through its parent, e.g. `navigation.navigate('Root', { screen: 'Details' })`
The screen is only rendered in some cases (e.g. after login)
fixes: Compare the name you navigate to with the name in <Stack.Screen>
For nested navigators, navigate to the parent with { screen: '...' }

patterns: Couldn't find a navigation object\. Is your component inside
errors.title: useNavigation() was called outside the navigation tree.
causes: The component isn't rendered inside <NavigationContainer> (for example in App.tsx, above it)
fixes: Use useNavigation only in components rendered by a screen, inside <NavigationContainer>
Need to navigate from outside? Use a navigation ref: createNavigationContainerRef
